author: PostgreSQL Global Development Group
observation: -X excludes startup files; -1 wraps -c/-f and rolls back on failure when ON_ERROR_STOP is set; explicit transaction commands interfere.
application: Use single transaction wrapper and fail-fast, without nested transaction control.

limitations: Connection loss at commit can leave outcome unknown; no runtime test.

author: PostgreSQL Global Development Group
observation: TRUNCATE is transactional but not MVCC-safe for snapshots predating truncation.

application: Coordinate or lock all input tables before acquiring snapshot; do not rely on RR alone with loader TRUNCATE.
inference: Coordinate or lock all input tables before acquiring snapshot; do not rely on RR alone with loader TRUNCATE.

author: PostgreSQL Global Development Group
observation: READ COMMITTED can read a new snapshot on each statement; REPEATABLE READ uses a transaction snapshot and can require retries.
application: Choose a controlled build snapshot and record input generation.
inference: Choose a controlled build snapshot and record input generation.
limitations: TRUNCATE has a documented special case; snapshot is not an external source version.

author: PostgreSQL Global Development Group
observation: Explicit table locks wait for conflicting locks and persist until transaction end; lock order and isolation affect safe usage.
application: Acquire suitable locks before snapshot, use timeout and deterministic order when reload cannot be excluded.
inference: Acquire suitable locks before snapshot, use timeout and deterministic order when reload cannot be excluded.
limitations: Permissions and blocking costs need local validation; locks across all tables must precede input reads.
task: Design and implement only after review: locks
acceptance_check: Concurrent fixture verifies both lock acquisition orders and timeout.
verification_method: Actually executed: read Description and Notes; proposed: Concurrent fixture verifies both lock acquisition orders and timeout.
